needs.text: Ruler v2: a calibration dataset the agent may run freely for identification, separate from dev (today it identifies from dev runs, so dev is both its training data and its score; holdout still checks it).

needs.text: Ruler v2: link and gearbox compliance in the twin, before stiffer gains count as a win.

needs.ask: Which gain rung should graduate to the real arm?
needs.text: Which gain rung should graduate to the real arm? Frontier, each rung identified at its own gains (dev mm): x1 `p5s-fric2-pass2` 0.070 (same energy as p4s, 12× better than p4s's 0.848) · x2 `p5s-kp2-pass2` 0.045 · x4 `p5s-pass3` 0.031 (energy +24 %, saturation 0.014 %). The twin cannot say how much stiffness the real UR5e/moteus loop tolerates; recommendation: x1 or x2.

needs.ask: Ruler or tooling: a sanctioned *calibration run*, so identification stops being fitted on the dev tasks it is scored on
needs.text: Ruler or tooling: a sanctioned *calibration run* (an excitation trajectory a solution may run through the boundary before the tasks, without `deployment.plant()`), so identification stops being fitted on the dev tasks it is scored on. Today the only data are dev run records; holdout says it transfers (dev 0.031 / holdout 0.031) but the scheme reads as fitting on the test set.

needs.ask: Ruler v2: the twin has no link/gearbox compliance or structural resonance, so board stiffness costs nothing here but the kd-noise energy
needs.text: Ruler v2: the twin has no link/gearbox compliance or structural resonance, so board stiffness costs nothing here but the kd-noise energy (+8.6 % at kp ×2). Without a gain-related gate (a resonance mode in the plant, an energy or torque-ripple gate, or a cap on sent stiffness), the search will drift to the stiffest gains the saturation gate allows. `p5s-kp2` and anything stiffer should be read with that in mind.

ideas.title: Identify the gravity error from the *joint errors*
ideas.text: ~~Identify the gravity error from the *joint errors*~~ → `p5s-grav` 0.097 mm dev (holdout 0.126), admissible, better on 41/42 tasks. (kp·e is a clean torque-error signal; the board's tau carries ±10 N·m of quantisation buzz). Regressing kp·e on the given model's own gravity term explains most of elbow (0.45 → 0.25 N·m) and w1 (0.094 → 0.035) and part of lift (1.08 → 0.90; with sin/cos of q2..q4 → 0.48). Expect: lift/elbow/w1 biases gone, ~10-20 %. Got −60 %.

# Leave it running overnight

## Observed

The black box is not reliable yet: it cannot be left to keep running through the night.

## Desired

Leave the search running overnight and find it still going, its record intact, in the morning.

## Why

> [!ai] claude-code (pick-trajgen box agent), from tests/test_runs_overnight.py
> AGENTS.md already promised that state lives in files, so any session can stop at any point and the next resumes.
> Nothing held that promise, and a run on 2026-11-25 with under 8 % of memory free broke it three ways:
> - **A killed worker was scored.** `multiprocessing.Pool` replaced the workers the machine killed without a word, so
>   the evaluation waited out its whole backstop deadline (160 s on four 1 s tasks; about 25 min on the dev split)
>   and then wrote each lost task as a failed `completed`. The machine's kill went into the ledger as the
>   controller's failure. Now the pool breaks at once, nothing is written, and `tta evaluate` exits 75 ("evaluate
>   again"); the score repeats bit for bit ([`tests/test_ruler_determinism.py`](../tests/test_ruler_determinism.py)).
> - **A torn ledger line would stop every command.** A row cut off by a crash made `ledger.rows()` raise. Now only a
>   torn last line is skipped, the next append cuts it off first, and a bad line with rows after it still raises.
> - **A half-written scorecard, run record, PROGRESS.md or status.json** stopped the next step that read it. Every
>   file `tta` writes now goes through `files.write_text`: a temporary file, flushed, renamed over the old one.
>
> [`tests/test_runs_overnight.py`](../tests/test_runs_overnight.py) holds all three. Each test failed before its fix.
> Still open: the search itself is driven by an agent session. When that session ends overnight, nothing here starts
> the next one; that is the driver's job, outside this repo.

# UR5e speed coverage and tracking

## Observed

Coverage exposed instantaneous joint speed distributions. Comparison combined a single nominal full-speed cohort with an automatic axis extending past 1.0. The site linked the older dataset target cards.

## Desired

Show the distribution of nominal time scales in stock Coverage. Show each controller’s tracking error across matched trajectories in tenth-speed buckets, with the first bucket at 0.1 and the axis ending at 1.0. Link the current stock Targets workbench and make it possible to open the exact charts from a report.

## Why

> [!ai] A nominal tape scale answers a different question from the time a joint spends near its limit. The same target paths at each speed make the comparison interpretable. The full-speed ranking and detailed recorded runs retain their existing provenance.

study.title: What made p5s-pass3 good
study.method: Fawcett & Hoos 2016 ablation (leave-one-out, add-one-in, greedy path); path choices on a surrogate (Biedenkapp et al. 2017), every step measured

ablation_study.findings:
- **Frozen, timing is most of it.** Removing the bus lookahead from p5s-pass3 makes it ×20.3 worse (0.636 mm), the board's lead ×9.1 (0.285 mm), both together ×23.8 (0.747 mm): one timing fix, not two (interaction ×0.13).
- **Refit, one identification pass re-learns it.** One `identify_pass.py` pass on each frozen variant's own dev runs: without the bus lookahead 0.0338 mm (×1.08), without the board's lead 0.0317 (×1.01), without identified friction 0.0316 (×1.007). Frozen leave-one-out overstates parts that a later fit can absorb.
- **Stiff gains are the part nothing replaces**: ×5.0 frozen, ×2.6 refit, and +24 % motor energy. Twin-only until it has compliance (ideas.md).
- **Late parts pay at the end.** The chord correction did −0.6 % when found and ×1.009 alone on p5s, yet removing it from the best costs ×1.45.
- **Greedy path (every step measured):** bus lookahead 0.595 → stiff gains 0.339 → board's lead 0.130 → friction 0.089 → gravity 0.078 → chord 0.053 → re-identification 0.036 → second friction pass 0.035 → velocity lag 0.031 mm. The first three give ×7.5 of the ×31.
- **A cheap point the search never visited:** bus lookahead + board's lead + stiff gains, `abl-path3+lead`: 0.130 mm in 23 runtime code lines with no identified model (the search's p5s-bus-enc: 0.393 mm in 20).
- **Method.** Fawcett & Hoos 2016: leave-one-out from the best, add-one-in from p5s, the greedy path. Path steps 2-7 were chosen on a surrogate (Biedenkapp et al. 2017; additive + Hamming-kernel ridge on log10 error, leave-one-out error ×1.56) and then measured; steps 1, 8 and 9 compared every candidate. Frozen = every other part keeps p5s-pass3's identified weights ([`ablations/pass3-2026-11-24/make_variant.py`](pass3-2026-11-24/make_variant.py), which reproduces the 11 lineage solutions to ≤ 4e-12). 30 new solutions, all admissible, none better than p5s-pass3. Shapley values on the pages are model-based estimates.

notes.bus: ×20 worse when removed with everything else frozen, ×1.08 after one refit pass: the joint-error identification fits a torque proportional to qd, which is what a timing error looks like. Alone on p5s it is still the biggest single step (−39 %).
notes.lead: ×9.1 frozen, ×1.01 refit. With the bus lookahead it is one timing fix: removing both costs ×23.8, not the ×184 the two alone multiply to.
notes.fric: ×3.0 frozen, ×1.007 refit: the later passes' friction basis spans it, so a refit re-learns it.
notes.chord: −0.6 % when the search took it, ×1.009 alone on p5s, ×1.45 when removed from the best: it only paid once the larger errors were gone. Not in the identification basis (it is a qdd term), so no refit was run.
notes.grav: −60 % when found; ×2.0 when removed from the best (frozen). Refit not measured; its 13 gravity shapes are inside passes 4 and 5's basis, so a refit would likely re-learn most of it, as it did for friction.
notes.stiff: The one part a refit cannot replace: ×5.0 frozen (p5s-pass3-g1), ×2.6 after a refit at the boards' own gains. It is also the energy cost: +433 J over the dev tasks (+24 %). Transfer risk: the twin has no compliance.
notes.reid: ×1.39 when removed (passes 4 and 5, fitted at kp ×4). p5s-onefit merged the passes into one model.json at equal error: 34 fewer runtime lines.
notes.p5s-onefit: refactor at equal error (Δ < 1e-13 mm): the four fits merged into one model.json, 34 fewer runtime code lines and 160 fewer stored numbers

overall.unit: log10 of the error; a drop of d is a factor 10**d; shares are d / log10(base / target)

methods.name: Removed from the best (leave-one-out)
methods.line: How many times worse p5s-pass3 gets with this part taken out and every other identified number frozen.

methods.name: Removed, then refit
methods.line: The same, after one identification pass on the variant's own runs (4 of 9 parts measured).

methods.name: Added alone to the base (add-one-in)
methods.line: How many times better p5s gets with only this part added.

methods.name: Its step on the ablation path
methods.line: The drop at the step where the greedy path adds it (steps 2-7 chosen on a surrogate, every step measured).

methods.name: Average over the measured orders
methods.line: Its average step over every order of adding the nine parts in which every intermediate set was measured. Exact for those orders; they are not a random sample of the 362,880 orders.

methods.name: Shapley value (fair share)
methods.line: Its average step over all 362,880 orders; the 474 sets nobody ran come from the surrogate. Error: jackknife over the measured sets.

methods.name: fANOVA main effect and total effect
methods.line: Share of the error's variance over all 512 sets (log10) explained by this part alone, and by everything it is in (its interactions too). On the same surrogate table; error: jackknife.

analysis._note:
---
study: pass3-2026-11-24
title: What made p5s-pass3 good
base: p5s
target: p5s-pass3
objective: tool_track_rms_mm
split: dev
removal: frozen
date: 2026-11-24
method: Fawcett & Hoos 2016 ablation (leave-one-out, add-one-in, greedy path); path choices on a surrogate (Biedenkapp et al. 2017), every step measured
---

# What made p5s-pass3 good

The search condensed: one section per step of the target's lineage that changed a component, in the order the search took them, with what removing it from the end costs and what it does alone. Steps that changed no component are listed under *Not a component*. The builder adds every number from the ledger.

## + lookahead = bus delay — [p5s-bus](../solutions/p5s-bus/)

- key: `bus`
- idea: "Coulomb ff with the bus's own lookahead, not the calibration's"
- without it at the end: [abl-no-bus](../solutions/abl-no-bus/) (frozen) · [abl-no-bus-refit](../solutions/abl-no-bus-refit/) (refit)
- alone on the base: [p5s-bus](../solutions/p5s-bus/)

×20 worse when removed with everything else frozen, ×1.08 after one refit pass: the joint-error identification fits a torque proportional to qd, which is what a timing error looks like. Alone on p5s it is still the biggest single step (−39 %).

## + minus the board's lead — [p5s-bus-enc](../solutions/p5s-bus-enc/)

- key: `lead`
- idea: "Take the board's own lead out of the lookahead"
- without it at the end: [abl-no-lead](../solutions/abl-no-lead/) (frozen) · [abl-no-lead-refit](../solutions/abl-no-lead-refit/) (refit)
- alone on the base: [abl-p5s+lead](../solutions/abl-p5s+lead/)

×9.1 frozen, ×1.01 refit. With the bus lookahead it is one timing fix: removing both costs ×23.8, not the ×184 the two alone multiply to.

## + identified friction — [p5s-fric](../solutions/p5s-fric/)

- key: `fric`
- idea: "Identify per-joint Coulomb + viscous from dev run records"
- without it at the end: [abl-no-fric](../solutions/abl-no-fric/) (frozen) · [abl-no-fric-refit](../solutions/abl-no-fric-refit/) (refit)
- alone on the base: [abl-p5s+fric](../solutions/abl-p5s+fric/)

×3.0 frozen, ×1.007 refit: the later passes' friction basis spans it, so a refit re-learns it.

## + chord correction — [p5s-chord](../solutions/p5s-chord/)

- key: `chord`
- idea: "Move the position target off the chord"
- without it at the end: [abl-no-chord](../solutions/abl-no-chord/) (frozen)
- alone on the base: [abl-p5s+chord](../solutions/abl-p5s+chord/)

−0.6 % when the search took it, ×1.009 alone on p5s, ×1.45 when removed from the best: it only paid once the larger errors were gone. Not in the identification basis (it is a qdd term), so no refit was run.

## + gravity identification — [p5s-grav](../solutions/p5s-grav/)

- key: `grav`
- idea: "Identify the gravity error from the *joint errors*"
- without it at the end: [abl-no-grav](../solutions/abl-no-grav/) (frozen)
- alone on the base: [abl-p5s+grav](../solutions/abl-p5s+grav/)

−60 % when found; ×2.0 when removed from the best (frozen). Refit not measured; its 13 gravity shapes are inside passes 4 and 5's basis, so a refit would likely re-learn most of it, as it did for friction.

## + second friction pass — [p5s-fric2](../solutions/p5s-fric2/)

- key: `fric2`
- idea: "Second friction pass against the target velocity, from joint errors"
- without it at the end: [abl-no-fric2](../solutions/abl-no-fric2/) (frozen)
- alone on the base: [abl-p5s+fric2](../solutions/abl-p5s+fric2/)

×1.13 when removed: small now.

## + stiff gains (kp ×4) — [p5s-kp2](../solutions/p5s-kp2/), [p5s-kp4](../solutions/p5s-kp4/)

- key: `stiff`
- idea: "Stiffer board gains (kp ×2, kd ×√2) on top of the identified models"
- without it at the end: [p5s-pass3-g1](../solutions/p5s-pass3-g1/) (frozen) · [abl-no-stiff-refit](../solutions/abl-no-stiff-refit/) (refit)
- alone on the base: [abl-p5s+stiff](../solutions/abl-p5s+stiff/)

The one part a refit cannot replace: ×5.0 frozen (p5s-pass3-g1), ×2.6 after a refit at the boards' own gains. It is also the energy cost: +433 J over the dev tasks (+24 %). Transfer risk: the twin has no compliance.

## + velocity-lag term — [p5s-vlag](../solutions/p5s-vlag/)

- key: `vlag`
- idea: "Same joint-error identification for the inertia terms"
- without it at the end: [abl-no-vlag](../solutions/abl-no-vlag/) (frozen)
- alone on the base: [abl-p5s+vlag](../solutions/abl-p5s+vlag/)

×1.12 when removed: small now.

## + re-identification at kp ×4 — [p5s-pass2](../solutions/p5s-pass2/), [p5s-pass3](../solutions/p5s-pass3/)

- key: `reid`
- idea: "Re-identify friction + gravity from joint errors at the current (kp ×4) gains"
- without it at the end: [p5s-vlag](../solutions/p5s-vlag/) (frozen)
- alone on the base: [abl-p5s+reid](../solutions/abl-p5s+reid/)

×1.39 when removed (passes 4 and 5, fitted at kp ×4). p5s-onefit merged the passes into one model.json at equal error: 34 fewer runtime lines.

## Not a component

- [p5s-onefit](../solutions/p5s-onefit/) — refactor at equal error (Δ < 1e-13 mm): the four fits merged into one model.json, 34 fewer runtime code lines and 160 fewer stored numbers

| [abl-path7+reid](../solutions/abl-path7+reid/) | 73 | 138 |
| [p5s-kp2](../solutions/p5s-kp2/) | 86 | 162 |
| [p5s-pass2](../solutions/p5s-pass2/) | 110 | 288 |
| [p5s-onefit](../solutions/p5s-onefit/) | 76 | 128 |

## Findings

- **Frozen, timing is most of it.** Removing the bus lookahead from p5s-pass3 makes it ×20.3 worse (0.636 mm), the board's lead ×9.1 (0.285 mm), both together ×23.8 (0.747 mm): one timing fix, not two (interaction ×0.13).
- **Refit, one identification pass re-learns it.** One `identify_pass.py` pass on each frozen variant's own dev runs: without the bus lookahead 0.0338 mm (×1.08), without the board's lead 0.0317 (×1.01), without identified friction 0.0316 (×1.007). Frozen leave-one-out overstates parts that a later fit can absorb.
- **Stiff gains are the part nothing replaces**: ×5.0 frozen, ×2.6 refit, and +24 % motor energy. Twin-only until it has compliance (ideas.md).
- **Late parts pay at the end.** The chord correction did −0.6 % when found and ×1.009 alone on p5s, yet removing it from the best costs ×1.45.
- **Greedy path (every step measured):** bus lookahead 0.595 → stiff gains 0.339 → board's lead 0.130 → friction 0.089 → gravity 0.078 → chord 0.053 → re-identification 0.036 → second friction pass 0.035 → velocity lag 0.031 mm. The first three give ×7.5 of the ×31.
- **A cheap point the search never visited:** bus lookahead + board's lead + stiff gains, `abl-path3+lead`: 0.130 mm in 23 runtime code lines with no identified model (the search's p5s-bus-enc: 0.393 mm in 20).
- **Method.** Fawcett & Hoos 2016: leave-one-out from the best, add-one-in from p5s, the greedy path. Path steps 2-7 were chosen on a surrogate (Biedenkapp et al. 2017; additive + Hamming-kernel ridge on log10 error, leave-one-out error ×1.56) and then measured; steps 1, 8 and 9 compared every candidate. Frozen = every other part keeps p5s-pass3's identified weights ([`ablations/pass3-2026-11-24/make_variant.py`](pass3-2026-11-24/make_variant.py), which reproduces the 11 lineage solutions to ≤ 4e-12). 30 new solutions, all admissible, none better than p5s-pass3. Shapley values on the pages are model-based estimates.

# O1.1 The boundary

## Requirement

> **The boundary is robot_msgs `JointTrajectory` + `JointState` in, `ServoCommand` out** (robot_controllers' contract
> §2), at the deployment's host rate over its bus. A moteus board takes a `ServoCommand` as is; a UR servoJ stream is
> one with position only; UR's direct torque is one with feed-forward only. The solution may use any of those fields.

From [OBJECTIVES.md §1 The black box](../OBJECTIVES.md#1-the-black-box), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

A solution is one function, `build(trajectory, deployment)`, that returns a controller. Every host tick the controller
is handed the arm's `JointState` and returns a `ServoCommand` (and a dict of its own diagnostics). Those are the only
two doors: everything the solution learns about the arm comes in as joint states, and everything it does goes out as a
servo command, in the message types a moteus board or a UR arm already takes. A controller that wins here is wired the
way a real arm is, so moving it to one changes no interface.

The rate and the bus belong to the deployment ([O2.1](O2.1-deployment-ur5e-alone.md)): a solution decides *what* to
send each tick, never *when* the tick runs or how long its command takes to arrive.

## Why

> WHY frozen (Zach, 2026-11-24): *"BEFORE I even take a look at kind what is going on inside … finalize the API, what is
> going in and out, what are the evaluation metrics, and how are they calculated."* The arm_motion_bench contract was
> amended 16 times in four days (v3.1 → v3.16), and two benches scored the same UR5e about 1000× apart
> (< 0.05 mm vs 2.0 mm), because they drew the boundary in different places. One frozen ruler fixes both.

That is OBJECTIVES.md's own WHY for the frozen ruler. Drawing the boundary once, at the messages a real arm takes, is
what makes two scores comparable. Zach's words are filed as feedback:
[freeze the ruler first](../feedback/2026-11-24-freeze-the-ruler-first.md).

## How it is checked

The [evaluator tests](../tests/test_ruler_evaluate.py) run a real UR5e simulation and check that the controller is
built from a `JointTrajectory` and receives `JointState` at the deployment's 50 Hz cadence. A raw array, an array
paired with diagnostics, and a `ServoCommand` missing a joint each fail `completed`
([O4.2](O4.2-gate-completed.md)).

requirements.name: O1.2 What a solution may know
requirements.statement:
**What a solution may know (clarified 2026-11-24, before any agent-written solution; no score changes):** it learns
about the robot only through the boundary, exactly as on a real arm: the deployment's public fields (joint names,
rates, bus, caps, limits, tool FK), the robot models robot_controllers *gives* the arm with the deployment's model
error (`base_scenario(arm).model_error`, 10 % on every link), and its own experiments run through the boundary
(commands in, joint states out: dev runs, or a calibration run such as robot_controllers' bus calibration). It never
reads the plant's parameters (`UR5E_TRUTH`, the plant's MjModel, its masses, friction or armature), never calls
`deployment.plant()`, and never uses a model with less error than it was given.
A solution never edits this file, [`datasets/`](../datasets/) or [`src/trajectory_tracking_agent/ruler/`](../src/trajectory_tracking_agent/ruler/).

From [OBJECTIVES.md §1 The black box](../OBJECTIVES.md#1-the-black-box), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

# O1.2 What a solution may know

## Requirement

> **What a solution may know (clarified 2026-11-24, before any agent-written solution; no score changes):** it learns
> about the robot only through the boundary, exactly as on a real arm: the deployment's public fields (joint names,
> rates, bus, caps, limits, tool FK), the robot models robot_controllers *gives* the arm with the deployment's model
> error (`base_scenario(arm).model_error`, 10 % on every link), and its own experiments run through the boundary
> (commands in, joint states out: dev runs, or a calibration run such as robot_controllers' bus calibration). It never
> reads the plant's parameters (`UR5E_TRUTH`, the plant's MjModel, its masses, friction or armature), never calls
> `deployment.plant()`, and never uses a model with less error than it was given.
>
> A solution never edits this file, [`datasets/`](../datasets/) or [`src/trajectory_tracking_agent/ruler/`](../src/trajectory_tracking_agent/ruler/).

From [OBJECTIVES.md §1 The black box](../OBJECTIVES.md#1-the-black-box), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

A solution plays by a real arm's rules. It may read what any integrator could read off the arm's datasheet and wiring
(the deployment's public fields), start from the robot models it is given, which carry 10 % error on every link, and
learn the rest from its own runs through the boundary. It may not read the simulator's truth: the plant's parameters,
its MuJoCo model or the plant object itself. Nor may it peek at the scorer (the ruler) or the holdout tapes (CONTRACT
§2), or edit the ruler, the dataset or OBJECTIVES.md.

The generation-1 solutions identify friction and gravity from their own dev runs. That is allowed, because those data
came through the boundary; [ideas.md](../ideas.md) asks for a separate calibration run so identification stops being
fitted on the tasks it is scored on.

## Why

> WHY: a gain that comes from knowing the simulator's truth can't transfer to a real arm
> ([simulator exploitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reward_hacking));
> [`tests/test_solutions_honest.py`](../tests/test_solutions_honest.py) checks every solution's source for it.

(OBJECTIVES.md §1.) The search is only worth running if what it finds works on a robot whose truth nobody knows.

## How it is checked

- [`tests/test_solutions_honest.py`](../tests/test_solutions_honest.py) reads every `.py` in every solution folder (helper scripts too, since gen-1 solutions
  identify their models with scripts beside `solution.py`) and fails on each direct route to the truth: `UR5E_TRUTH`, the
  plant object, the plant's MuJoCo model, a model error of zero, the ruler, the holdout split.
- `test_a_solution_importing_the_ruler_is_refused`: a solution that imports the ruler fails closed and `evaluate`
  refuses it.
- `test_check_source_names_dataset_reads_but_not_docstrings`: a path into [`datasets/`](../datasets/) is flagged; a docstring that
  merely says "holdout" is not.

A source check, not a proof, as the honesty test says of itself: it catches the direct routes. The dispatcher also
reads each agent-written solution's diff.

requirements.name: O1.3 The trajectory is given
requirements.statement:

# O1.3 The trajectory is given

## Requirement

> **A solution cannot retime, reshape or skip the trajectory** (layer 3 of the arm_motion_bench v2.0 layers: the
> trajectory and the robot are given; the levers are the torque and the controller).

From [OBJECTIVES.md §1 The black box](../OBJECTIVES.md#1-the-black-box), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

The tape is the target. A solution may look ahead along it (feed-forward, a lookahead), but the score compares the
measured tool point with the tape's own target at the tape's own instants ([O4.1](O4.1-objective-tool-track-rms.md)).
Slowing down, cutting a corner or skipping a via point all show up as tracking error, and the speed is fixed at 1.0
([O3.1](O3.1-dataset-workspace-v2.md)).

## Why

It keeps two problems apart: making a trajectory (planning and timing it) and following one. This agent works only on
the second; in OBJECTIVES.md's words, "the trajectory and the robot are given; the levers are the torque and the
controller". If a solution could retime the tape, a slower trajectory would read as better tracking.

## How it is checked

The [evaluator](../src/trajectory_tracking_agent/evaluate.py) gives the controller its own message with immutable
sample buffers and keeps the dataset tape as the scoring reference. The [evaluator tests](../tests/test_ruler_evaluate.py)
check the original sample times, positions, and file checksum after a controller tries to track at half speed. They
also verify that direct writes and attempts to reopen any sample array for writing fail `completed`.

# O2.1 Deployment ur5e_alone

## Requirement

> | Part | Value | Source |
> |---|---|---|
> | Robot + plant | MuJoCo Menagerie UR5e, the "truth" plant (armature, dry friction, damping), floor-mounted | `robot_controllers.bench.ur5e` (`Ur5ePlant`, `UR5E_TRUTH`) |
> | Servo boards | the moteus board model with the UR5e datasheet caps (150 ×3, 28 ×3 N·m) | `robot_controllers.bench.ur5e.ur5e_board_config()` |
> | Host rate | 50 Hz (the rig's) | robot_controllers base scenario |
> | Bus | the datasheet bus for six devices | `robot_controllers.timing` / `BusTiming.from_datasheet` |
> | Scene | the arm alone on a floor (floor plane z = 0 at the base) | arm_motion_bench `ur5e_alone` (CONTRACT v3.16) |
> | Tool point | the flange site `tool`, 0.1 m along wrist_3 | `robot_controllers.bench.ur5e.tool_position` |
>
> The plant, boards and bus are imported from robot_controllers at a pinned version, never copied or edited here.
>
> **The deployment owns the rate and the bus**, never the solution: robot, scene, host rate, bus timing, the servo
> boards' model and caps.

From [OBJECTIVES.md §2 Deployment v1: `ur5e_alone`](../OBJECTIVES.md#2-deployment-v1-ur5e_alone), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

One fixed simulated world. The arm is MuJoCo Menagerie's UR5e with a "truth" plant (armature, dry friction, damping)
that no solution may read ([O1.2](O1.2-what-a-solution-may-know.md)). Each joint sits behind a moteus board model
carrying the UR5e's datasheet torque caps. The host ticks at 50 Hz and its commands travel a bus timed from the
datasheet, so a command lands late the way it would on the rig. The arm stands alone on a floor, and the tool point is
the flange site.

All of it is imported from robot_controllers at a pinned version, so the ruler cannot drift through a local edit.

## Why

Two benches once scored the same UR5e about 1000× apart because they drew the boundary in different places
(OBJECTIVES.md's WHY, quoted in [O1.1](O1.1-the-boundary.md)); owning the rate and the bus in the deployment, never in
the solution, is half of drawing it once.

The scene is Zach's: "just the UR", "UR with nothing around it" (2026-11-23, quoted in
[`datasets/ur5e_alone/workspace/v2/station.json`](../datasets/ur5e_alone/workspace/v2/station.json)). Filed as feedback:
[just the UR](../feedback/2026-11-23-just-the-ur.md).

## How it is checked

- `test_deployment_is_objectives_section_2`: the deployment's host rate, bus, board model, caps, floor and limits are
  this table's.
- `test_the_mount_matches_the_datasets_floor_mount_up_to_a_yaw`: the plant stands where the dataset's stored tool
  positions say the arm stood (the same base on the same floor, turned about the vertical axis).
- `test_link_points_put_the_base_on_the_floor_and_the_tool_last`: the points the floor gate reads start at the base on
  the floor and end at the tool point.
- `tests/test_ruler_determinism.py::test_the_deployment_calibration_is_the_pinned_one`: the deployment's calibrated
  lookahead is the pinned robot_controllers value, so a dependency bump that moves it is caught.

requirements.statement:
- The UR5e's whole workspace, arm alone on the floor: joint A→B moves, straight tool lines, via points and the two
  ISO 9283 tasks. **dev** = seed 1001 (42 tasks), **holdout** = seed 2001 (12 tasks).
- Timed by bam_ruckig (jerk-limited, time-optimal) at the UR5e's limits. **Speed 1.0 only** in ruler v1.
- Frozen copy of arm_motion_bench [`datasets/ur5e_alone/workspace/v2`](../datasets/ur5e_alone/workspace/v2/) (its `manifest.json` sha256s), with the timed
  tapes at speed 1.0 committed (bam_ruckig is private, so the public repo ships tapes, not the generator).
  `tta verify` re-checks every sha256.

From [OBJECTIVES.md §3 The dataset v1: `ur5e_alone/workspace/v2`](../OBJECTIVES.md#3-the-dataset-v1-ur5e_aloneworkspacev2), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

# O3.1 Dataset workspace/v2

## Requirement

> - The UR5e's whole workspace, arm alone on the floor: joint A→B moves, straight tool lines, via points and the two
>   ISO 9283 tasks. **dev** = seed 1001 (42 tasks), **holdout** = seed 2001 (12 tasks).
> - Timed by bam_ruckig (jerk-limited, time-optimal) at the UR5e's limits. **Speed 1.0 only** in ruler v1.
> - Frozen copy of arm_motion_bench [`datasets/ur5e_alone/workspace/v2`](../datasets/ur5e_alone/workspace/v2/) (its `manifest.json` sha256s), with the timed
>   tapes at speed 1.0 committed (bam_ruckig is private, so the public repo ships tapes, not the generator).
>   `tta verify` re-checks every sha256.

From [OBJECTIVES.md §3 The dataset v1: `ur5e_alone/workspace/v2`](../OBJECTIVES.md#3-the-dataset-v1-ur5e_aloneworkspacev2), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

The targets are fixed files. The dev split (42 tasks) is what a solution runs and is scored on; the holdout split
(12 tasks) is scored only to report a finished solution ([O4.8](O4.8-holdout-is-reporting-only.md)). Every tape was
timed once, jerk-limited and time-optimal at the UR5e's limits, at speed 1.0, and committed; nothing here re-times them.

## Why

A frozen copy of the tapes arm_motion_bench scores means a number here and a number there measure the same motions.
The tapes are committed rather than regenerated because the generator, bam_ruckig, is private and this repo is
public. A tape that changed by one byte would silently change every score, so every sha256 is re-checked.

## How it is checked

- `test_verify_*`: `tta verify`'s dataset check is clean, and it catches a changed tape, a new or a missing file, and a
  manifest rewritten to match a changed tape (each tape's sha256 must also be the one arm_motion_bench's manifest lists).
- `test_split_counts_and_order`: dev and holdout hold their task counts, in order.
- `test_every_tape_is_in_ur5e_joint_order_from_rest`: every tape is in the UR5e's joint order, starts and ends at rest,
  and carries no feed-forward (a solution brings its own).

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

For each dev task: at every target sample where the target is moving, take the distance between where the tool is (the
FK of the measured joints) and where it should be at that same instant (the FK of the target joints); the task's
number is the RMS of those distances, in millimetres. The objective is the median of the task numbers.

- *At the same instant*: lagging behind the target is error, even on the right path.
- *Moving samples only*: a long rest before or after a move does not dilute the number.
- *Median*: one odd task does not decide the score; every task still has to pass every gate
  ([O4.7](O4.7-fail-closed-admissible.md)).
- *Through the FK of the joints*: the measurement a real arm's encoders give, never a simulator body pose a real arm
  doesn't have.

## Why

One number makes the search a search: lower is better, and nothing else ranks a solution
([O4.9](O4.9-ranking.md), [O4.10](O4.10-diagnostics-never-optimized.md)). How it is calculated is fixed for the same
reason the boundary is:

> WHY frozen (Zach, 2026-11-24): *"BEFORE I even take a look at kind what is going on inside … finalize the API, what is
> going in and out, what are the evaluation metrics, and how are they calculated."* The arm_motion_bench contract was
> amended 16 times in four days (v3.1 → v3.16), and two benches scored the same UR5e about 1000× apart
> (< 0.05 mm vs 2.0 mm), because they drew the boundary in different places. One frozen ruler fixes both.

Filed as feedback: [freeze the ruler first](../feedback/2026-11-24-freeze-the-ruler-first.md).

- `test_moving_mask_*`: what counts as moving, just above and just below each threshold, by tool speed alone and by
  joint speed alone.

  with no moving samples is NaN.
- `test_objective_*`: the median of odd and even counts; any NaN makes it NaN; no tasks is NaN.
- `test_metrics_compose_on_rest_move_rest`: the metrics agree on one rest, move, rest motion.
- [`tests/test_ruler_oracle.py`](../tests/test_ruler_oracle.py): an independent oracle. The episode is re-run straight through robot_controllers, the
  tool pose comes from MuJoCo's own site rather than the ruler's FK, the error from robot_msgs, and the result must
  agree with the ruler's objective.
- `test_measured_tool_is_fk_of_the_plants_joints_on_the_targets_grid`: both tool points are the deployment's FK of
  joint angles, on the target's own instants.

requirements.description:
# O4.2 Gate: completed

## Requirement

> | `completed` | no exception, no NaN command, the run reaches the trajectory's end and settles | a crash is not a score |

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

The run has to finish cleanly. In `evaluate.py`'s words: the build and every tick raise nothing, no command field
that drives torque is NaN or infinite, the host loop logs no abort and the physics does not diverge, the task stays
inside its wall-time box (CONTRACT §4), the run reaches the trajectory's end with finite joints, and it settles: every
tool error over the trajectory's last 0.1 s is within Zach's 1 mm band (`SETTLE_BAND_MM`, the same band as
[O4.3](O4.3-gate-stop-error.md)).

## Why

"A crash is not a score" (OBJECTIVES.md §4). A controller that blew up halfway would otherwise be scored on the samples
it did run, and could look good doing it. The settle band is Zach's 1 mm tool gate again:
[a 1 mm tool gate](../feedback/2026-11-11-tool-gate-1mm.md).

## How it is checked

- `test_gate_completed`: the gate reads the `completed` flag and fails closed.
- `test_a_build_that_raises_fails_every_gate`: a `build` that raises fails `completed` and every other gate.
- `test_a_nan_command_fails_completed`: a NaN in a torque-driving command field fails it.
- `test_the_time_box_fails_completed`: a controller too slow for its wall-time box fails it.

# O4.3 Gate: stop error ≤ 1 mm

## Requirement

> | `stop_error_max_mm` | ≤ 1.0 mm: target vs mean tool position over each stop's last 0.1 s (a stop = target at rest ≥ 0.2 s) | Zach's standing 1 mm tool gate (2026-11-11) |

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

A stop is any stretch where the target rests for at least 0.2 s. At each stop, average the measured tool position over
the stop's last 0.1 s and take its distance from the target; the task's number is its worst stop, and it must be at
most 1.0 mm. The mean lets a small zero-mean buzz average out; a steady offset does not. A task with no stops scores
0.0 and passes (CONTRACT §6).

## Why

Zach's standing 1 mm tool gate (2026-11-11), as OBJECTIVES.md names it. The objective rewards following the path while
it moves; this gate makes sure the arm also arrives. Filed as feedback:
[a 1 mm tool gate](../feedback/2026-11-11-tool-gate-1mm.md).

## How it is checked

- `test_stop_windows_*`: what a stop is, on both sides of the 0.2 s threshold, at the 50 Hz host rate, at the start
  and the end of a trajectory.
- `test_stop_error_*`: only the last 0.1 s counts; the worst stop against its own target; millimetres out of metres
  in; a zero-mean oscillation averages out; no stops is 0.0.
- `test_gate_stop_error_max_mm*`: the gate's threshold.
- `test_a_controller_that_never_moves_fails_the_stop_gate`: a real run that holds still fails it.

requirements.description:
# O4.4 Gate: saturation ≤ 2 %

## Requirement

> | `saturation_share_pct` | ≤ 2 %: share of samples where any joint torque is ≥ 98 % of its cap | speed bought with saturation doesn't transfer |

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

Count the samples in which any joint's torque, by magnitude, is at or above 98 % of that joint's cap (the datasheet
caps of [O2.1](O2.1-deployment-ur5e-alone.md)); that share of the run must be at most 2 %. The evaluator counts it on
every physics sample, not only the target's, so a spike between two target samples still counts.

## Why

"Speed bought with saturation doesn't transfer" (OBJECTIVES.md §4). A controller that rides the torque cap can track
well in a twin that knows the cap exactly; on a real arm it has no margin left for whatever the model got wrong.

## How it is checked

- `test_saturation_*`: exactly 0.98 of the cap counts and just under does not; a negative torque counts by magnitude;
  each joint against its own cap; a sample counts once whichever joint saturates.
- `test_gate_saturation*`: the gate's threshold.

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.
requirements.description:
# O4.5 Gate: limit violations = 0

## Requirement

> | `limit_violations` | 0 samples outside a position limit or above 1.05 × a velocity limit | — |

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

No sample may put a joint outside its position limits or move it faster than 1.05 × its velocity limit. A joint
exactly on a position limit, or exactly at 1.05 × its velocity limit, does not count.

## Why

OBJECTIVES.md gives no reason (its Why cell is "—"). A reading, not the ruler's: a real arm's own controller faults on
these, so a solution that crosses them would not run there; the headroom on velocity leaves room for a tracking
overshoot on tapes timed right at the UR5e's limits ([O3.1](O3.1-dataset-workspace-v2.md)).

## How it is checked

- `test_limit_*`: on the limit does not count and outside does; above 1.05 × counts, between the limit and 1.05 × does
  not; each joint against its own limits; samples are counted, not violations.

requirements.description:
# O4.6 Gate: floor clearance

## Requirement

> | `floor_clearance` | 0 samples with the tool point or any link origin below the floor plane | the bare plant has no contacts, so collision with the scene is checked geometrically |

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

The simulated arm has no contacts, so nothing physical stops it from swinging through the floor. The gate checks the
geometry instead: on no sample may the tool point or any link origin be below the floor plane (z = 0 at the base,
[O2.1](O2.1-deployment-ur5e-alone.md)). A point exactly on the floor does not count; a NaN pose fails.

## Why

"The bare plant has no contacts, so collision with the scene is checked geometrically" (OBJECTIVES.md §4). Without it a
solution could cut through the floor and score well doing it. Full collision detection is deferred
([O5.3](O5.3-collision-detection.md)).

## How it is checked

- `test_floor_*`: below counts and on the floor does not; samples are counted, not points; a custom floor height.
- `test_gate_floor_clearance*`: the gate reads the violation count, not a verdict's name.

requirements.description:
# O4.7 Fail closed, admissible

## Requirement

> **Gates (per task; a solution is *admissible* only if every dev task passes every gate):**
>
> **Every verdict fails closed** (arm_motion_bench v3.11): a missing or NaN value is a failed gate, never a pass.

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

A gate whose value is missing or NaN has failed. A solution is admissible only when every dev task passes all five
gates ([O4.2](O4.2-gate-completed.md) to [O4.6](O4.6-gate-floor-clearance.md)); with no tasks, it is not admissible.
Only admissible solutions can be the best ([O4.9](O4.9-ranking.md)).

## Why

Fail closed comes from arm_motion_bench v3.11 (OBJECTIVES.md §4). A reading of why: a gate that passes on missing data
passes exactly the runs that broke worst, since a crash produces no numbers.

## How it is checked

- `test_gate_verdicts_*`: every gate fails on a missing or NaN value and passes on good values.
- `test_gates_tuple_is_frozen`: the five gates, by name and order.
- `test_admissible_*`: every task and every gate; one failure, a task missing a gate, or no tasks at all is not
  admissible.
- `test_rows_from_a_failed_task_are_json_safe`: a crashed task's row still records failed verdicts.

**Holdout** is scored only by `evaluate(..., split="holdout")` for reporting. Choosing between solutions on holdout
is a bug (it would make holdout a second dev set). The leaderboard shows holdout − dev beside each admissible solution.

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.
requirements.description:
# O4.8 Holdout is reporting only

## Requirement

> **Holdout** is scored only by `evaluate(..., split="holdout")` for reporting. Choosing between solutions on holdout
> is a bug (it would make holdout a second dev set). The leaderboard shows holdout − dev beside each admissible solution.

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

The holdout tasks never run in a dev evaluation, and no solution reads them ([O1.2](O1.2-what-a-solution-may-know.md)).
An agent scores holdout only to report a finished solution, and never picks between solutions by it. The leaderboard
puts holdout − dev beside each admissible solution, so a dev gain that does not carry to unseen tasks shows.

## Why

"It would make holdout a second dev set" (OBJECTIVES.md §4): once a choice reads holdout, it stops being unseen.

## How it is checked

- `test_holdout_is_never_scored_by_a_dev_evaluation`: the dev split holds only dev tasks and shares none with holdout.

That test checks the splits, not the agent. That no agent selects on holdout is a rule in AGENTS.md ("Never select on
holdout"), which the dispatcher reads for in each solution's change and lineage.

requirements.name: O4.9 Ranking
requirements.statement:
**Ranking:** admissible solutions by `tool_track_rms_mm` (lower first); then the rest by gate pass rate, then
objective. The *best* solution is the lowest-objective admissible one.

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.
requirements.description:
# O4.9 Ranking

## Requirement

> **Ranking:** admissible solutions by `tool_track_rms_mm` (lower first); then the rest by gate pass rate, then
> objective. The *best* solution is the lowest-objective admissible one.

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

Admissible solutions come first, best objective first. The rest follow by how many of their task gates pass, then by
objective. The best solution is the admissible one with the lowest objective; when no solution is admissible, there is
no best, and the progress log says so.

Solutions an ablation study made (tagged `ablation`) are measurements of a finished line's parts, not search steps:
the best, PROGRESS.md and status.json leave them out (see the feedback below).

## Why

Gates first, objective second: a fast controller that breaks a gate is not better than a slower one that passes them
all. Ablation variants stay out of the best because "ablation variants must not read as search progress"
(Zach, 2026-11-24, as [`tools/progress_chart.py`](../tools/progress_chart.py) quotes the rule). Filed as feedback:
[ablations are not progress](../feedback/2026-11-24-ablations-are-not-progress.md).

## How it is checked

- `test_ranking_is_objectives_section_4`: a ledger of admissible and failing solutions ranks in this order, and the
  best is the admissible one with the lowest objective.
- `test_no_admissible_solution_is_said_plainly`: no admissible solution means no best, said in words.

requirements.description:
# O4.10 Diagnostics are never optimized

## Requirement

> **Diagnostics** (reported, never optimized): `tool_track_max_mm`, `joint_track_rms_deg` (worst joint),
> `tool_lag_ms`, `stop_error_mm` (median), `saturation_share_pct`, `energy_j` (positive mechanical work, labelled
> "motor energy"), `tool_jerk_rms_m_s3`, `host_compute_ms_p95` (the solution's own `tick` time), `wall_time_s`.

From [OBJECTIVES.md §4 The score](../OBJECTIVES.md#4-the-score), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

Every scorecard carries these numbers. They explain a score (where the error is, how much lag, how hard the motors
work, how long `tick` takes); they never rank one. An agent reads them to decide what to try next, but a solution that
only improves a diagnostic has not improved.

## Why

OBJECTIVES.md says only "reported, never optimized". A reading, not the ruler's: one objective keeps the search honest,
and every extra number it optimized would be another one to game (Goodhart's law); the gates hold the limits that
matter.

## How it is checked

**No test**, and none required: it is a *should* about what the agent optimizes, not about code. What the code does
check is the ranking, which reads only admissibility, gate pass rate and the objective
([O4.9](O4.9-ranking.md)), never a diagnostic.

# O5.1 Speeds below 1.0

## Requirement

> Deferred to ruler v2 (named so nobody thinks they were forgotten)
>
> Speeds below 1.0 (the sweep)

From [OBJECTIVES.md §5 Deferred to ruler v2](../OBJECTIVES.md#5-deferred-to-ruler-v2-named-so-nobody-thinks-they-were-forgotten), ruler v1. OBJECTIVES.md is the frozen ruler and the one source of every number; this note explains it and never overrides it.

## What it means

Ruler v1 scores every task at speed 1.0 only ([O3.1](O3.1-dataset-workspace-v2.md)): the tapes are timed right at the
UR5e's limits. Slower runs of the same tasks (the sweep) are not scored.

## Why

Named in §5 "so nobody thinks they were forgotten". [ideas.md](../ideas.md)'s *Suggestions for Zach* asks for slower
speeds in ruler v2, so a gain at full speed can't hide a loss at low speed.

## How it is checked

Deferred: not part of ruler v1, so nothing tests it and its status is *deferred*. It becomes a requirement only in ruler v2, which OBJECTIVES.md says is a new section and a re-score of every solution in [`solutions/`](../solutions/).

## Requirement

Everything here is simulation. A solution reaches a real arm only by graduating out of the search into a separate

AGENTS.md: "Sim only. The real arm is a separate stage; nothing here opens a bus." Which line graduates first is in
[ideas.md](../ideas.md)'s *Suggestions for Zach* (the dispatcher's default: `p5s-kp2-pass2`, with `p5s-fric2-pass2` as
the fallback); flying it is a hardware step for Zach.

## What it means

Today the measured tool point is the FK of the joint encoders ([O4.1](O4.1-objective-tool-track-rms.md)). A camera
would see where the tool really is, including what bends between the joints and the tool, which the FK cannot.

## Why

Named in §5 "so nobody thinks they were forgotten". [ideas.md](../ideas.md)'s *Suggestions for Zach* asks for link
and gearbox compliance in the twin for ruler v2; until the twin bends, encoder FK and a camera would agree.

## How it is checked

Deferred: not part of ruler v1, so nothing tests it and its status is *deferred*. It becomes a requirement only in ruler v2, which OBJECTIVES.md says is a new section and a re-score of every solution in [`solutions/`](../solutions/).
